mechanism_narrative: Increasing GDP indicates strong economic demand, leading to higher S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: GDP growth does not correlate with positive S&P returns.

mechanism_narrative: Rising unemployment rate signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P returns.
failure_condition: Unemployment rise does not predict negative S&P returns.

mechanism_narrative: Both unemployment and employment increases indicate labor market strength, boosting S&P.
failure_condition: No positive correlation between labor metrics and S&P returns.

mechanism_narrative: High federal funds rate in tightening cycles may reduce S&P returns.
failure_condition: High FEDFUNDS does not predict negative S&P returns.

mechanism_narrative: High inflation reduces purchasing power, leading to lower S&P returns.
failure_condition: Inflation does not correlate with negative S&P returns.

mechanism_narrative: Strong industrial production indicates economic strength, boosting S&P.
failure_condition: Industrial production growth does not predict positive S&P returns.

mechanism_narrative: Housing starts and retail sales indicate strong demand, boosting S&P.
failure_condition: No positive correlation between housing/retail and S&P returns.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansion, high unemployment and rates signal S&P decline.
failure_condition: No negative correlation between labor/monetary metrics and S&P returns.
